title: Agent-to-agent message envelope (v1)
description: One message between two students' personal agents. This never travels through Cubbie: Cubbie cannot text anyone but its own student, so agent-to-agent traffic runs over the CampusOS service (see docs/adr/0001). Every field here exists because routing a message safely requires knowing who sent it, who they speak for, how far their authority runs, and how much they may disclose.

trace_id.description: Correlates every message in one negotiation across services and logs. Required: an untraceable message cannot be audited, and the privacy claim rests on the audit trail.

sender.description: The agent process that produced this message. Distinct from the student it represents: an agent is software with an identity of its own, and conflating the two is how an agent ends up speaking for someone who never authorised it.

represented_student.description: Who the sender speaks for, as an opaque per-negotiation pseudonym. Never a name or email.

scope.description: The limits of this agent's authority, as granted by its student. The receiver MUST refuse an intent not listed in actions, and MUST refuse a message whose scope has expired. Authority is explicit, bounded and expiring -- never implied by possession of a token.

max_disclosure_level.description: The ceiling the student set. The envelope's disclosure_level may be lower, never higher. Required: an absent ceiling used to validate, which made 'unspecified authority' indistinguishable from 'full authority' -- the wrong default for the field that bounds disclosure.

granted_by.description: How the student authorised this. 'standing' is a preference set once; 'per_negotiation' was confirmed for this negotiation specifically. Anything that books, sends or commits requires per_negotiation.

disclosure_level.description: What this message is permitted to reveal. Same ladder as availability.schema.json. At or below scope.max_disclosure_level, and at or above the nested payload.availability.disclosure_level -- both enforced structurally in allOf below, and again by the service at runtime against the authenticated grant.

intent.description: propose: offer a time. counter: reject the offer and offer another. accept: agree to the offer on the table. reject: decline without countering. escalate: hand the decision to the human, which is a normal outcome and not an error.

reason_code.description: A closed vocabulary, deliberately. Free-text reasons are how private information escapes a system that is otherwise careful: 'conflict' is routable, 'I have therapy at 2' is a leak.

note_for_own_student.description: Text shown ONLY to the student this agent represents, never transmitted to another student's agent. The service strips it on egress.

allOf.$comment: A propose or counter must carry something to react to.
A reject or escalate must say why, in the closed vocabulary.

A counter or accept answers a specific prior message. Without in_reply_to, 'accept' means 'the offer on the table' -- ambiguous the moment two proposals are open, and the ambiguity resolves into someone being committed to a time they did not agree to.

Accepting commits the student to a time. A standing preference set once, in advance, is not consent to this specific commitment; scope.granted_by must say the student confirmed this negotiation. This is the schema half of the rule the service also enforces.

THE DISCLOSURE LADDER, ACROSS THE WHOLE MESSAGE. Three levels appear in one envelope -- the ceiling the student granted (scope.max_disclosure_level), what this message claims to reveal (disclosure_level), and what the availability payload actually carries (payload.availability.disclosure_level). Each must be at or below the one above it. Checking them in isolation, as this schema first did, lets a free_busy message carry a full payload with a 'therapy' label: every part is internally consistent and the whole leaks. JSON Schema cannot compare enums, so the ordering is written out. none < free_busy < category < full.
Ceiling free_busy: the message may claim none or free_busy.
Message none: the payload may not carry an availability envelope above none either.
Message free_busy: the nested envelope may not be category or full.
Message category: the nested envelope may not be full.
